Moody's Did Not Downgrade France and Peripheral Premiums are Narrower, but the Euro Struggles to Find Traction
posts.text: There are two impulses today. First, defying expectations, Moody’s did not downgrade its assessment of French credit, which remains above S&P and Fitch’s ratings. With a show of force by the government, French protests were less violent. French bonds have rallied and the peripheral premium has narrowed. Yet, the euro has found little meaningful traction. Second, and also defying expectations, Brazilian President Lula appears to have beaten Bolsonaro in a nailbiter. In the futures market the Brazilian real has been sold.
